none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Minimize Φ(x)=max_y f(x,y); neither convexity in x nor concavity in y is required.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: Uniform one-sided maximization PL condition: 2μ(Φ(x)−f(x,y))≤‖∇_y f(x,y)‖². No PL condition is imposed on Φ or the minimizing variable.

problem_class.label: saddle_point
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimax problem with an attained global inner maximum for every x; the output is an outer point x.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: The same query returns the full exact joint gradient, independently of history and seed.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each joint query z returns the exact value f(z).

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact full Hessian oracle: each query also returns D(∇f)(z). Value, gradient, and Hessian are bundled into one oracle call.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E and F are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces; joint queries use the Euclidean product norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The joint gradient is globally L-Lipschitz and its derivative is globally ρ-Lipschitz in operator norm. All parameters and starting points are public: 0<μ≤L, ρ>0, ε>0, Δ,D≥0. Initialization satisfies Φ(x0)−inf_x Φ(x)≤Δ and Φ(x0)−f(x0,y0)≤D.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NonconvexPLSecondOrder.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Both stationarity inequalities hold jointly almost surely under the output law, within the supplied fixed oracle budget.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: Φ and ∇Φ must be differentiable everywhere. At the returned x, for every v, ⟨v,D(∇Φ)(x)v⟩≥−√(100ρ√(L/μ)(4+L/μ)ε)‖v‖².

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup seeks second-order stationarity and global twice differentiability of the primal value function under inner PL geometry without inner concavity, using exact joint second-order information.
